title: the Rajasuya
hook: the four younger brothers ride out to the four directions; in the far north, Arjuna reaches a land with nothing to conquer

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Rajasuya's road went through a prison door: the kings freed, and Jarasandha's son put on his father's throne. Did you leave someone something real? Day seven hundred fifty-six.

Back at Indraprastha, the plan gets bigger. If kings are going to come and honor Yudhishthira, the brothers will have to go and meet them first. So the younger four divide the world. Arjuna rides north. Bhima rides east. Sahadeva rides south. Nakula rides west. Yudhishthira stays home, in the hall, with Dhaumya and his friends around him. Each brother will come back with the tribute of kings. And one of them will come back from a place where there was nothing to win.
screen: `NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, WEST.` → `YUDHISHTHIRA STAYS HOME.` → `A PLACE WITH NOTHING TO WIN.`

segments.voice: The text follows each brother in turn: kingdoms, battles, and kings who submit or welcome them and send gifts. It's a long march, told region by region. But one moment at its northern edge stands apart. Arjuna rides on, past mountain after mountain, until he reaches the land of the Northern Kurus. At the gate, powerful guards stop him, and they speak to him kindly. You can't conquer this place, they say. There's nothing here to fight. Even if you came in, you couldn't see anything with human eyes. We're pleased with you. Tell us what you want. And Arjuna doesn't push. He doesn't try the gate. He says, simply: I want my brother Yudhishthira to be sovereign. If this land is closed to humans, I won't enter. Give something as tribute, and I'll go. They give him fine cloth, ornaments and skins, and he turns back. Set it beside the battles around it. The conquest of the directions is about winning recognition for one king. And at the far edge of it, Arjuna, who won Draupadi with his bow, meets a land he can't win, and is content to ask. Now look back over this week. A father's message through Narada. A sage's warning, and a king who wanted honest counsel. Krishna naming Jarasandha. A birth in two halves. A midnight meeting, a long fight, a prison opened, a throne given back. And now the brothers coming home from four directions with the world's gifts. Everything is ready. Tomorrow, the Rajasuya itself.
screen: `FOUR BROTHERS, FOUR DIRECTIONS.` · `THE NORTHERN KURUS' GATE.` · `NOTHING HERE TO CONQUER.` · `ARJUNA ASKS, AND TURNS BACK.` · then, large: `CONTENT TO ASK.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and let the breath find its own pace. Bring to mind something you've been pushing at, a door that won't open. Picture yourself at it, the way Arjuna stood at that northern gate. Now imagine asking for what you really need, instead of forcing your way in. What would you ask? Let the answer come in its own time. If nothing comes, just rest at the gate. The bell holds the time.
The Rajasuya. Today, the brothers ride to the four directions to win kings' tribute for it, and at the northern edge Arjuna simply asks.
Your line: the Rajasuya. Today, at one door that won't open, try asking instead of pushing. Day seven hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: The word digvijaya, conquest of the directions, outlived the epic: tradition uses it for the travels of the teacher Shankara, whose victories are told as debates won across India rather than battles.

original.note: Sanskrit digvijaya: 'victory over the directions', the name of the section in which the brothers ride out.

trapdoor: what you thought: a war of conquest.
what it means: a campaign to win other kings' recognition, so they'll come to the Rajasuya.
what a scholar hears: at its northern edge the campaign meets a land that can't be won, and Arjuna leaves with tribute freely given.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Digvijaya Parva (the four brothers ride to the four directions; Arjuna at the land of the Northern Kurus)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm the assignment of directions: Arjuna north, Bhima east, Sahadeva south, Nakula west; Yudhishthira remaining at Indraprastha with Dhaumya and friends.
Confirm the Northern Kurus (Uttara Kurus) episode: kindly, powerful gatekeepers, 'nothing to conquer', 'nothing seen by human eyes', Arjuna's reply, and the tribute of cloth, ornaments and skins.
Arjuna winning Draupadi with his bow refers back to the swayamvara days.
Digvijaya glossed as 'victory over the directions' (dik + vijaya); this is a compound meaning, not a contested etymology, but confirm.
Week-end look back covers days 750–756. Day 757 (another writer) covers the rite itself.
howItsDone: confirm the phrasing about Shankara's digvijaya (the Shankara-digvijaya hagiographies).

Editor pass: replaced howItsDone, which repeated day 749's guardians-of-the-directions note, with the later use of digvijaya for Shankara's travels; cut 'the shape of the whole campaign in one scene', since the rest of the campaign is battles and the northern episode is the exception.
